ac:rich-text-body.p: This page is part of the company Database Security Configuration Policy (SEC-POL-DB-001). Its requirements are mandatory for every database in scope. Deviations need an approved entry in the DB Security – Exceptions Register. CIS Benchmarks and Tenable audit files are the technical basis and assessment method; where this policy differs from CIS, this policy applies.

p: This policy sets the minimum security configuration for every company database. It protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of company and customer data, and gives auditors one place to see each requirement, how Tenable assesses it, and the current compliance status.

ul.li: Every database in scope must be configured to meet the controls on its platform page before it goes into production, and must stay compliant for its whole life.
Database configuration compliance must be assessed with Tenable using the approved audit files on the schedule in section 6.
Failed controls must be remediated within the timelines in section 7, or covered by an approved, time-limited exception.
New database platforms or major versions must not go into production until a platform page for them is approved.

p: All database instances owned or operated by the company, or operated for it by a third party, in production, DR, UAT and development environments, on-premises or in the cloud (IaaS). Managed database services (PaaS) are in scope for the controls the company can configure.

td.p: Oracle Database (single instance, RAC, Data Guard; CDB and PDBs)
CIS Oracle Database 19c Benchmark (use the 23ai benchmark for 23ai)
Microsoft SQL Server (Database Engine, on Windows or Linux; Always On availability groups)
MySQL Community / Enterprise Server (InnoDB Cluster, replication)
CIS Oracle MySQL Community / Enterprise Server 8.0 Benchmark
MongoDB Community / Enterprise Server (replica sets, sharded clusters)
IBM Db2 for Linux, UNIX and Windows (LUW), including HADR
No CIS Benchmark is published. Company baseline derived from the Teradata Vantage Security Administration guide and DB-COM controls

p.em: [e.g., embedded databases inside vendor appliances, developer workstations, decommissioned systems]

td.p: Approves the policy and exceptions rated CRITICAL; reports compliance to the risk committee
Build databases to this policy, remediate findings, keep platform pages and control values current
Maintain scan policies, audit files and credentials; run scans; publish compliance results
Approve access, classify data, accept risk for exceptions on their systems
Receive and monitor database audit logs in the SIEM
Independently test compliance with this policy

p: Every platform page implements these company-wide requirements. Platform pages may be stricter, never weaker.

td.p: Run a vendor-supported release and apply security patches within the patch SLA.
No end-of-support versions; latest security patch level minus one at most
Change, lock or remove every vendor default and sample account.
No account with a default or blank password
Human administrators authenticate with named accounts through central directory (AD / LDAP / Kerberos) where the platform supports it.
No shared admin logons; break-glass account vaulted in PAM
Local database accounts follow the corporate password standard.
Min. 14 characters, complexity on, lockout after ≤ 5 failures, expiry ≤ 90 days for human accounts, reuse history ≥ 10
Grant privileges through roles on least privilege. Nothing beyond vendor defaults to PUBLIC / guest.
Admin roles limited to the approved DBA group; quarterly access review
Encrypt all client and replication traffic.
TLS 1.2 or higher (or native network encryption with AES-256); plaintext listeners disabled
Encrypt data at rest for databases classified Confidential or higher.
TDE / native encryption, or encrypted volumes with keys outside the DB host
Audit logons (success and failure), privilege and security changes, and DDL. Forward to the SIEM.
Audit enabled; retained ≥ 12 months (90 days online)
Expose the database only to the application and admin networks that need it.
Bound to required interfaces; host / network firewall allow-list
Disable features that execute OS commands, read files or open network connections unless approved.
Off by default; approved exceptions only
Run database services under a dedicated, non-root / non-administrator account. No credentials in clear text in files or scripts.
Dedicated service account; config files readable only by the service account
Encrypted backups; restore test at least annually
Tenable Policy Compliance Auditing (credentialed), with the audit files listed on each platform page
CIS-based Tenable audit files, tailored to the company values on the platform pages. Tailored copies are version-controlled and the version is recorded on each platform page
Dedicated read-only scan account per platform (privileges on each platform page), stored in Tenable / PAM, never a DBA account
Production: monthly and after every major change or upgrade. Non-production: quarterly. New builds: before go-live
Asset lists synchronized from the CMDB database inventory; every instance in scope is scanned
100% of CRITICAL and HIGH controls passing (or covered by an exception); ≥ 95% of all controls
Published to the compliance dashboard below; failed controls raise remediation tickets for the owning team
Controls marked MANUAL / PARTIAL are reviewed quarterly; evidence is attached to the review ticket
Direct path to unauthorized access or data exposure
Significant weakness in authentication, privileges, encryption or auditing
Hardening gap with limited direct exposure

p.em: Timelines run from the Tenable scan date that first reports the failure. Align them with the corporate vulnerability management standard before approval.

td.p: The Tenable audit fully assesses the requirement; PASS / FAIL comes from the scan
Tenable collects the data but a reviewer completes the check (e.g., against an approved list)
A DBA or reviewer collects evidence by hand during the review
A custom audit check is being built
Cannot be assessed from the database or host; evidence is collected another way

p: Platform controls that implement each common baseline requirement. A gap means the requirement is assessed by another process (e.g., backups by the backup standard, host hardening by the OS standard) or a control still has to be written.

td.p: Run a vendor-supported release and apply security patches within the patch SLA.
Change, lock or remove every vendor default and sample account.
Human administrators authenticate with named accounts through central directory (AD / LDAP / Kerberos) where the platform supports it.
Local database accounts follow the corporate password standard.
Grant privileges through roles on least privilege. Nothing beyond vendor defaults to PUBLIC / guest.
Encrypt all client and replication traffic.
Encrypt data at rest for databases classified Confidential or higher.
Audit logons (success and failure), privilege and security changes, and DDL. Forward to the SIEM.
Expose the database only to the application and admin networks that need it.
Disable features that execute OS commands, read files or open network connections unless approved.
Run database services under a dedicated, non-root / non-administrator account. No credentials in clear text in files or scripts.

ul.li: Any control that cannot be met needs an exception in DB Security – Exceptions Register before the remediation deadline.
Exceptions have a named risk owner, a compensating control and an expiry date of at most 12 months.
CRITICAL exceptions are approved by the policy owner; others by the Head of Database Engineering and the application owner.
Approved exceptions are applied as exclusions in Tenable so they are not reported as failures, and are re-reviewed at expiry.

p: Overdue findings without an approved exception are escalated to the system owner's management and reported to the risk committee. Databases with open CRITICAL findings may be isolated from the network. Wilful breach of this policy may lead to disciplinary action under the company code of conduct.

Format: <PREFIX>-<DOMAIN>-<NNN>, for example ORA-AAA-001. Prefixes: ORA Oracle, MSSQL Microsoft SQL Server, MYSQL MySQL, MONGO MongoDB, DB2 IBM Db2, TD Teradata. Control IDs are never renumbered or reused; retired controls are struck through with RETIRED vX.Y in Comments.

td.p: Vendor-supported release, security patches / release updates applied
Default accounts, password policy, lockout, central authentication
Least privilege, PUBLIC / guest rights, admin role membership
TLS in transit, encryption at rest, key management
Database audit trail, failed / successful logons, forwarding to SIEM
Listener / bind address, ports, remote administration
Dangerous features disabled, sample databases removed, secure parameters
Service account, file permissions, no clear-text credentials on disk

ul.li: This policy is reviewed at least annually and approved by the policy owner.
Platform pages are also reviewed after a new CIS Benchmark or Tenable audit file release, a major database version, or an audit finding.
When a new benchmark version is adopted, record the benchmark and audit file versions on the platform page and update the CIS Reference column.
CIS Benchmarks: https://www.cisecurity.org/cis-benchmarks (basis for control values; licence terms apply to benchmark content)
